title: Inner product of polynomial evaluations
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be mutually independent real random variables with finite fourth moments, mean zero, and second moment one. For coefficient families $F,G: \mathcal P(\{0,\ldots,n-1\})\to\mathbb R$, define $F(X)=\sum_S F(S)\prod_{i\in S}X_i$ and likewise $G(X)$. Then $\mathbb E[F(X)G(X)]=\sum_S F(S)G(S)$.
hypotheses_covered: the random variables are mutually independent
each random variable has mean zero
each random variable has second moment one
replaced: Let $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ be mutually independent real random variables on a probability space, each in $L^4$, centered, and with second moment $1$. For real coefficient families $F,G$ indexed by subsets of $[n]$, writing $F(X)=\sum_S F(S)\prod_{i\in S}X_i$ and similarly for $G$, one has $\E[F(X)G(X)]=\sum_S F(S)G(S)$.
